How much does brake pad replacement cost?

New pads on one axle — what it costs, and what moves the price:

$335–$394

Labor $122–$179 · parts $213–$215

Bay Area: no published metro-specific figure found — the national range is the honest reference.

Why quotes run $150 to $600

Rotors
Pads alone: $150–$300 per axle. Add rotors and you're at $300–$600 — new rotors run $50–$200 each, and many shops skip resurfacing now.
Pad material
Ceramic pads cost $40–$120 a set; economy organic $20–$50. Ceramic lasts longer, runs quieter, and doesn't dust up your wheels.
Labor rates
The job books about an hour per axle. Independent shops charge $80–$150/hr; dealerships $150–$250/hr — same pads, very different bill.
Vehicle
A Civic's brake job costs less than a truck's or a BMW's. Heavy vehicles and performance brakes sit at the top — sometimes $350–$400 per axle for pads alone.

What the extra money buys

Pads only
$150–$300

New friction material on your existing rotors. Fine when rotors are smooth, thick enough, and not warped — the shop measures, you don't guess.

Pads + rotors
$300–$600

New discs and pads together. The right call when you feel pulsing, see deep grooves, or the rotors are below minimum thickness.

Bottom line: don't replace rotors on schedule — replace them on measurement. A shop that quotes rotors without measuring is selling, not diagnosing.

Common questions

How long do brake pads last?

25,000 to 75,000 miles depending on the car, the pad, and how you drive. City stop-and-go eats pads; highway cruising barely touches them.

Do I need to replace front and rear together?

No. Fronts do 60–70% of the braking and wear 2–3 times faster. Replace the axle that's worn; leave the other alone.

Can I skip the rotors and just do pads?

Yes, if the rotors are smooth, unwarped, and above minimum thickness. If they're grooved or pulsing, new pads on bad rotors is money wasted.

How long does a brake job take?

About an hour per axle for pads; add another half hour or so per axle with rotors. It's a same-day job.

Every car prices differently.

The range above is a national average. Your price depends on the car, the pads, and whether the rotors are coming along. Take a photo of your brake quote or the worn pads in Brightglow for an estimate on the actual car, and to compare local shops who've done the same work.
